Figure 3:Overview of the Intent Engine: a Multi-Source Data
Perception layer (Section3.1) feeds an
Intent Reasoning Core (Section3.2), built on a
Multi-Scale Intent Model and a Dreaming Mechanism, whose
hierarchical intent is consumed by Downstream Applications
(Section3.3).

Figure 4:Multi-source data perception in DREAM. A device-cloudF1F_{1}–F4F_{4}Traffic Funnel distills multi-source behavioral
evidence into compact behavior packs:F1F_{1}–F3F_{3}encode, gate, and
package behaviors on device, whileF4F_{4}enriches and re-admits them
in the cloud. The enriched bahavior pack feeds the Intent Reasoning Core to
maintain the hierarchical L0–L2 intent representation.
Figure 5:Overall architecture of the Intent Reasoning Core.

Figure 7:Request-time strategy orchestration. DREAM stores one semantic
strategy bundle and compiles it into stage-specific, guarded parameter
overrides. The production pipeline itself remains unchanged.

Figure 8:Offline policy training with production-path replay. The baseline
and strategy treatments are separate service calls. Repeated execution and
mean aggregation reduce serving noise before binary reward assignment.

Figure 9:Qualitative production trace through the DREAM control path.
(a) The Intent Engine supplies multiple concurrent hierarchical intent
cards; P3 is expanded only to expose the card schema. (b) MetaModel jointly summarizes the cards, diagnoses the user state, identifies the optimization objective, and emits bounded rank/re-rank control parameters. (c) The rank/re-rank pipeline applies the selected overrides and returns the product sequence.
